Andrew —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached are two working artifacts we will use for the formal RFP commit: (1) controls matrix mapping Redwood capabilities to NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act obligations, and (2) our regression sampling plan tailored for high-risk clinical workflows. High level summary below, attachments contain the implementation-level evidence and references.

High level:
- NIST/EU mapping: we map Controls to Implementation (runtime, dev lifecycle, monitoring) and Evidence (audit logs, eval snapshots, policy configs). We call out which capabilities are native to Redwood (e.g., KV cache isolation, model pinning, routing policies) vs. recommended customer controls for private deployments (e.g., VPC config, KMS).
- Regression sampling: baseline periodic sampling (weekly stratified random sampling across cohorts), triggered sampling on performance drift (automated retrigger when rolling AUC/ROC change > 1.5%), and heavy-tail sampling: we maintain a long-tail queue capturing flagged outputs (human-in-the-loop tags + automated anomaly detectors) and sample 1000+ events per quarter from that queue for manual review and eval regrading.
- Evidence: we can share SOC2 snapshot (redacted), retention policies, eval run logs, and a sample eval deck for the triage pipeline.

Next steps: 30-min sync next Tue/Wed works for our team. Please confirm a time and I'll send calendar invite.

Attachments: 20261211-redwood-controls-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), 20261211-regression-sampling-plan.pdf (pdf), redwood-soc2-snapshot-2026.txt (txt)

Regards,

Alex Martinez

Folks —

Forwarding Meridian's initial ask and the artifacts I attached to Andrew. Can you review the two attachments and call out any areas that need stronger evidence or different wording before we send a formal response? Specific items I'm after:
- Marissa: please check the control-to-evidence mapping for EU AI Act high-risk deployment obligations and confirm whether our suggested mitigations (traceability hooks, eval sampling quotas) map cleanly to Article 15/22 requirements.
- Neha: please validate the regression sampling math (sample sizes for rare-event tail sampling) and the triggered retrain thresholds; note that Meridian expects clinical triage sensitivity > 98% at baseline and wants to know how we measure and guard that.

Key open questions for the formal response:
1) We currently propose quarterly full long-tail review + weekly automated drift checks. Are we comfortable stating quarterly manual review as our recommended cadence for high-risk customers or should we make that a customer-configurable recommendation?
2) Evidence packaging: can we include a redacted SOC2 snapshot as-is, or do we need legal signoff for this prospect?
3) Do we want to offer a limited sample of evaluated outputs with human regrades as part of the initial procurement due diligence?

Please reply with notes inline. I will consolidate and send to Andrew by Monday EOD if we can get quick turn.

Thanks — Alex

Andrew / Alex / Neha —

Thanks for the clear framing. We've reviewed the attachments and made three focused updates to ensure the response will be procurement-ready:

1) Controls matrix (updated) — included explicit traceability to NIST AI RMF Core Functions (IDENTIFY/PROTECT/DETECT/RESPOND/RECOVER) and mapped EU AI Act obligations by clause. We added examples of "evidence artifacts" (audit log exports, eval snapshot ids, policy config hashes) and a short guidance note on redaction when sharing with external auditors.

2) Regression sampling plan (updated) — clarified stratified sampling approach for clinical triage:
   - Baseline: weekly stratified random sample of 1% of requests, minimum 500 records/week
   - Triggered: auto-trigger when rolling sensitivity falls by >1.5% over a 7-day window; triggered job will: 1) sample 5k records from recent 30-day window (stratified by cohort), 2) push to human regrade queue, 3) produce a regression report and recommended rollback/patch options.
   - Long-tail: maintain flagged-longtail queue; quarterly manual review sampling of 1,000+ flagged items with focused root-cause annotations.

3) Evidence & legal: we can share a redacted SOC2 snapshot now. For customer-specific audit packs (complete logs, unredacted configurations), we require an NDA + data access agreement. We've added a short paragraph in the response that captures these gating items and a recommended timeline for providing full artifacts (2–3 weeks after contractual NDA).

Action items / next steps:
- Alex: attach the updated artifacts from our shared drive (I exported the revised matrix and sampling plan to the Meridian folder).
- Alex / Neha: confirm the sample-size math in writing (Neha, any quick notes on power calculations would be great).
- Andrew: if you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough next Wed (22 Dec) at 10am ET.

We'll keep the language concise for procurement and include an annex with the technical appendix and evidence list.

Best,

Marissa Cole
